tasks.title: Shared integration test harness for a wiremock Sync API server
acceptance: `tests/support/mock_api.rs` exposes a `MockSyncApi` helper that starts a `wiremock::MockServer`, serves `POST /api/v1/sync` from a fixture, and returns its `base_url()`

`MockSyncApi` can be scripted per test: full-sync response, incremental response keyed by `sync_token`, 401, 429 with `Retry-After`, 5xx, and a transport drop (server shut down) - each with a named constructor
`MockSyncApi::received_commands()` returns the `commands` arrays of every request seen, so tests can assert a command was sent exactly once

`tests/support/env.rs` exposes a `TestHome` guard creating an isolated temp HOME/XDG config+data dir, pointing the binary at the mock base URL and a file-backed fake token (`tok_fake_abc123`), and removing the dir on drop
`Cargo.toml` gains only new `[dev-dependencies]` entries (wiremock, tempfile, assert_cmd/predicates as needed); no existing dependency pin or `rust-toolchain.toml` is modified
At least one smoke test in `tests/` uses the harness end to end and passes under `cargo test --all`
`cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass
tasks.context: Later epics (06 sync cycle, 05 offline queue, 11 CLI) each ship their own ad-hoc test setup; this task consolidates one harness every EPIC-12 test reuses. Follow the existing wiremock usage in `tests/sync_client.rs` and the fixture conventions in `tests/fixtures/`. Integration tests are separate binaries, so shared code must live in `tests/support/mod.rs` and be included via `mod support;`. No production code changes.

tasks.title: Integration suite: full offline to online cycle against the mock API
acceptance: First run against the mock performs a full sync (`sync_token: "*"`) and populates the local cache; a second run sends the stored `sync_token` and applies the incremental fixture
With the mock server stopped, a local mutation (add/complete) is queued durably and the process exits 0 reporting the offline state
Restarting the process with the mock server back up flushes the queue: `received_commands()` contains the queued command exactly once, and a replayed flush does not duplicate it (uuid idempotency)
A 401 response surfaces an unauthenticated error and does not clear the local cache; a 429 with `Retry-After` is retried and the cycle still succeeds
A server-generated `temp_id_mapping` replaces the local temp id in the cache, asserted by reading the cache after the flush
Every test is hermetic: isolated temp HOME, no network beyond the mock, no sleeps longer than 100ms, suite completes in under 30s
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: This is the acceptance-critical suite of the epic ('full offline→online cycle'). It depends in prose on EPIC-05 (queue), EPIC-06 (sync cycle) and EPIC-11 (non-interactive CLI entry points) being merged - prefer driving the CLI commands (`add`, `sync`) so the test stays decoupled from internal module paths. Keep fixtures small (a handful of projects/items) and free of real account data.

tasks.title: 5k-task dataset generator and perf benchmark harness
acceptance: `tests/support/dataset.rs` deterministically generates a 5000-item / 50-project dataset (fixed seed, fake names only) as both a sync response body and a prepopulated cache file
`tests/perf_gates.rs` measures and asserts: cold start to first frame < 500ms, input-to-render < 16ms (p95 over >=100 simulated key events), mocked sync request round trip < 2s p95 over >=20 requests
Measurements use the 5k dataset and a `TestBackend`-style headless render path, not a real terminal
Each gate prints the measured value and the threshold so CI logs show headroom
Thresholds live in named constants at the top of the file with a comment linking them to REQ-001
The perf tests are gated behind `#[ignore]` or a `PERF=1` env check so they do not slow the default `cargo test --all`, and the chosen mechanism is documented in the file header
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes
tasks.context: Depends in prose on EPIC-08/09 (rendering) for the render path and EPIC-06 for the sync cycle. Timing in CI is noisy: measure medians/p95 over repeats, warm up once before measuring, and avoid asserting on a single sample. Reuse `MockSyncApi` from T-1101 for the request-latency gate.

tasks.title: Automated log scan: no token or PII in the generated log file
acceptance: The test runs a full exercise (auth, sync against the mock, a queued mutation, logout) with `RUST_LOG=trace` and the log file redirected into the temp HOME

It greps the resulting log file for the fixture token `tok_fake_abc123` and asserts zero occurrences; it also asserts `***`/`REDACTED` appears at least once (proving the Secret helper ran, not that logging was silently disabled)
The log file is asserted non-empty and to contain at least one line per exercised phase, so a no-op log cannot pass the test
A second case asserts no fixture email, phone or raw task content marked as sensitive leaks into the log
A negative-control unit assertion proves the grep would catch a planted token in a sample string
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Epic acceptance: 'automated test greps the generated log file for the test token and asserts zero occurrences'. The `Secret<T>` helper and `REDACTED` marker in `src/log.rs` must not be modified (CLAUDE.md hard rule) - this test only observes them. Use only fake credentials.

tasks.title: Security integration tests: file permissions and HTTPS-only enforcement
acceptance: On unix, after first run the SQLite cache file, its `-wal`/`-shm` siblings and the file-backed token are asserted to be mode 0600 and their parent dirs 0700; the test is `#[cfg(unix)]` and skipped cleanly elsewhere
A pre-existing world-readable token file is either tightened or rejected with a clear error - whichever the code does is pinned by the test with a comment stating the chosen contract
`tests/security_https.rs` asserts an `http://` base URL is rejected with the `InsecureBaseUrl` error and no request is ever attempted (mock server records zero hits)
A `https://` base URL against the mock is accepted, proving the check is scheme-based and not a blanket block
Neither test writes outside its temp HOME
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: `InsecureBaseUrl` already exists in `ApiError` (see `src/error.rs`, EPIC-03). The permission expectations come from REQ-001 security requirements. Pure test task - if the code does not yet enforce 0600, stop and report rather than editing production files.

tasks.title: E2E: logout wipes everything and the next start behaves like first run
acceptance: Scenario: authenticate against the mock, sync, queue one offline mutation, run `logout`, then start again and re-authenticate

After `logout` the test asserts the token (keyring stub and file source), the SQLite cache, the pending queue and any sync-token state are all gone from the temp HOME; the directory listing is asserted explicitly
The post-logout restart sends `sync_token: "*"` (full sync), asserted via the mock's recorded requests
The previously queued offline mutation is NOT replayed after logout (asserted: zero commands in the post-logout requests)
`logout` exits 0 and prints a confirmation; a second `logout` on an already clean home also exits 0 (idempotent)
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Builds on the existing `src/auth/cache_wipe.rs` / `src/cli/logout.rs` from EPIC-02. Epic acceptance explicitly requires this verified both manually (T-1112) and in an integration test. Drive the real binary via `assert_cmd` so the test covers wiring, not internals.

tasks.title: CI: integration and perf-gate jobs on the existing workflow
acceptance: `ci.yml` keeps the existing fmt/clippy/unit jobs unchanged in behaviour and adds an `integration` job running the EPIC-12 integration and e2e suites, and a `perf` job running the ignored/`PERF=1` perf gates
Jobs run on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest via a matrix; the perf job runs on ubuntu-latest only, with a comment explaining the macOS runner's timing variance
Cargo registry/target caching is shared with the existing jobs; total added wall time is documented in a comment
A failing gate (clippy warning, failed integration assertion, or exceeded perf threshold) fails the overall workflow - no `continue-on-error`
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` is valid YAML (parsed in review) and the local commands it runs are reproducible verbatim from a developer machine
The commands remain identical to the ones documented in CLAUDE.md for fmt/clippy/test
tasks.context: Workflow-only change; no Rust source edits. Keep the existing job names so branch protection rules do not break. The deliberate-regression proof required by the epic acceptance is recorded separately in T-1113.

tasks.title: Packaging metadata and cargo install verification
acceptance: `[package]` gains `readme = "README.md"`, `repository`, `homepage`, `documentation`, `keywords`, `categories`, `rust-version` and `exclude` (docs/, .sdlc/, tests fixtures) so `cargo package` produces a lean crate
`cargo package --allow-dirty --no-verify` succeeds and the printed file list contains `src/`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` and excludes `docs/` and `.sdlc/`
A `install` CI step runs `cargo install --path . --locked --root $(mktemp -d)` on Linux and macOS and the resulting binary answers `--version` with the crate version
The binary links rustls and bundled SQLite only - the job asserts no `libssl`/`libsqlite3` dynamic dependency (ldd/otool check) so the single-binary promise is machine-checked
No existing dependency version pin, `Cargo.lock` entry or `rust-toolchain.toml` is changed
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all` pass
tasks.context: `Cargo.toml` already pins `reqwest` to rustls-only and `rusqlite` to `bundled` - this task proves those choices at the artifact level. Add a `LICENSE` file only if missing; the manifest already declares `license = "MIT"`. Metadata-only change, no src edits.

tasks.title: Release workflow: tagged Linux and macOS binary artifacts
acceptance: Workflow triggers on tags matching `v*.*.*` and on `workflow_dispatch` for dry runs
Matrix builds `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin`; each job produces `todoist-tui-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` plus a `.sha256` checksum file
Artifacts are attached to the GitHub Release created from the tag, with the release body taken from the matching CHANGELOG section
Builds run `--locked --release` and the workflow fails if `Cargo.lock` would change
A `workflow_dispatch` dry run uploads build artifacts but does not create or modify a release
Permissions are least-privilege (`contents: write` only on the publish job) and no secrets other than the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` are referenced
tasks.context: New workflow file only; do not modify `ci.yml` here (T-1107 owns it). Homebrew/AUR recipes are listed as optional in the epic and are deliberately deferred - note that in the workflow header comment. Never commit tokens; rely on the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

tasks.title: README: install, auth, keybindings, config reference, sync behaviour, troubleshooting
acceptance: Sections exist for: what it is, install (`cargo install`, release tarball, build from source), first-run auth and `logout`, keybindings, configuration reference, offline/sync behaviour, non-interactive CLI (`add`/`sync`/`today`), troubleshooting, and development/CI commands

The keybindings section is a single markdown table with `| Key | Context | Action |` columns listing every default binding, in a block delimited by `<!-- BEGIN KEYMAP -->` / `<!-- END KEYMAP -->` markers so T-1111 can parse it
The configuration reference is a table with `| Key | Type | Default | Description |` covering every key in the config model, delimited by `<!-- BEGIN CONFIG -->` / `<!-- END CONFIG -->`
Offline/sync section states: queued commands survive restart, flush is idempotent via uuid, `sync_token` drives incremental sync, and what happens on 401/429
Troubleshooting covers keyring unavailable (file fallback), log location and `RUST_LOG`, cache reset, and HTTPS-only errors
No real tokens, emails or account data appear anywhere; examples use `tok_fake_...` placeholders
Every shell command shown is copy-pasteable and matches the commands in CLAUDE.md / `ci.yml`
tasks.context: No README.md exists in the repo yet - this creates it. Content for keybindings/config comes from EPIC-08/09 (TUI) and `src/config/model.rs`. Keep the marker comments exact: the T-1111 drift test parses them. Documentation only, no code.

tasks.title: Drift test: documented keymap and config match the code defaults
acceptance: The test parses the `<!-- BEGIN KEYMAP -->` block of `README.md` and asserts the set of (key, context, action) rows equals the default keymap exported by the code - missing and extra rows are both failures, each reported by name
The test parses the `<!-- BEGIN CONFIG -->` block and asserts the documented key set and defaults equal the config model's keys and `Default` values
Failure messages name the exact offending binding/key and tell the author to update README.md, not to weaken the test
A malformed or missing marker block fails the test with a clear message rather than silently passing on zero rows
`cargo test --all` passes
tasks.context: Epic acceptance requires 'a test/script asserts the documented keymap matches the code's default keymap'. Depends in prose on EPIC-08/09 exposing the default keymap as iterable data; if it is not iterable, stop and report rather than editing TUI source from this task. Read README.md via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` so the test works from any cwd.

tasks.title: Manual test plan: real account checklist and terminal matrix
acceptance: Checklist covers: first-run auth, full sync, create/complete/edit/delete, offline mutations then reconnect, `logout` then fresh start, and each non-interactive CLI command
A terminal matrix table covers 80x24 and a large window, truecolor and 16-colour terminals, on Linux and macOS, with a pass/fail/notes column per combination
Setup section mandates a dedicated Todoist test project and an account that holds no real personal data; the doc explicitly forbids recording tokens, emails or real task content in results
Each check has an unambiguous expected result and a tick box, so a second person can execute the plan without reading code
A 'Results' section with date, version/commit, tester and outcome table is present and filled in for one executed run
Cross-links to README.md troubleshooting and to `docs/manual/epic-02-auth-checks.md` for the auth-specific checks
tasks.context: Follow the tone and structure of the existing `docs/manual/epic-02-auth-checks.md` and `epic-03-sync-api.md` (factual reference pages). The epic acceptance requires the plan to have been executed once with results recorded - leave the results table in place with a clear placeholder if execution is pending, and flag that in the PR description.

tasks.title: CHANGELOG and CI gate-regression verification record
acceptance: `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog + SemVer with an `Unreleased` section and a `0.1.0` entry summarising EPIC-01..EPIC-12 user-visible behaviour
Heading format matches what the release workflow (T-1109) extracts for release notes, and that contract is stated in both files
`docs/manual/epic-12-release-runbook.md` documents the tag-to-release steps, the artifact naming scheme, checksum verification, and the rollback/yank procedure

The runbook contains a 'Gate regression verification' section recording, for each gate (fmt, clippy, unit, integration, perf), the deliberate regression used, the CI run link or date, and the observed failure - proving the gates actually fail
No secrets, tokens or real account data appear in either file
Links from README.md install section to the runbook are valid relative paths
